report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of 5 of vendors.py: floor_check, _withheld_paths, council_env, council_cwd, run_managed, CouncilProfile, FORBIDDEN_ARG_FRAGMENTS, _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS, COUNCIL_PROFILES, _assert_profile_safe, CouncilAdapter class start.
risks: floor_check docstring | high | Claims path tier is killed by secret_floor_rule("", prompt) but this function does not call that; it calls secret_floor_rule(path, "") for each path. The claim is about a tempting call not used here; the code is consistent but the docstring warns about a pattern not present. | Verify that the docstring's warning is accurate by checking secret_floor_rule behavior elsewhere.

run_managed | medium | Uses ManagedProcess; if CancellationUnavailable or OSError occurs, returns spawn_error but does not ensure child process is killed. Docstring says 'Fail closed: a child we could not contain must never be left running.' but the except block does not attempt to kill any leftover process. | Confirm that ManagedProcess guarantees cleanup on context manager exit even if constructor fails.
run_managed | low | Uses time.sleep(0.02) in polling loop; may cause slight delay in timeout detection. | No action needed unless sub-second precision required.

council_cwd | medium | Raises ValueError if temp dir is inside repo_root, but only checks at creation; if repo_root is None, no check performed. Docstring says 'Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root' but only checks when repo_root is not None. | Confirm intended behavior: should it always check?
CouncilAdapter docstring | medium | Claims 'ask is the ONLY entry point' but the class is not fully defined in this chunk; no ask method is shown. | Verify that ask is defined in a later chunk.
CouncilAdapter docstring | low | Claims 'a refusal is a STATUS, not an exception' but STATUSES is not defined in this chunk. | Check STATUSES definition elsewhere.
todos: Verify that floor_check's docstring's warning about secret_floor_rule("", prompt) is not misleading.
Ensure run_managed's except block properly contains child processes.
Check council_cwd behavior when repo_root is None.
Complete CouncilAdapter class definition (ask method, STATUSES).

claims.text: secret_floor_rule("", prompt) kills the path tier outright: a patch that ADDS .env or config/id_rsa sails through, because the only trace of the filename is diff --git a/.env b/.env inside text, which no content regex matches.
claims.why: The claim references secret_floor_rule behavior not shown in this chunk. The function floor_check does not call secret_floor_rule("", prompt) with path empty except as a backstop; the claim warns against a pattern not present in this code.

claims.text: the channels are driven separately and PER FILE, exactly as the floor's own docstring requires
claims.why: floor_check iterates over evidence_paths and evidence_files separately, calling secret_floor_rule per file.

claims.text: evidence_paths -- every changed path (PatchArtifact.changed_paths) and every evidence file path, each through the PATH channel alone
claims.why: References PatchArtifact.changed_paths not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: evidence_files -- (path, text) pairs, both channels, per file
claims.why: The for loop calls secret_floor_rule(path, text or "") which checks both path and content.

claims.text: prompt -- a content-channel BACKSTOP for a credential pasted into the question itself. It is a backstop, never the whole check.
claims.why: The function calls secret_floor_rule("", prompt or "") only after per-file checks, and returns None if all pass.

claims.text: Returns the first FloorRefusal, or None. A hit means REFUSE -- there is no redact-and-send.
claims.why: The function returns a FloorRefusal as soon as a rule matches, or None at the end.

claims.text: Not a decision made by a default argument: an untrusted lane means OpenAI / Google get the allow-list, and every withheld path is named on the reply so a reader can see what the council did NOT see.
claims.why: References 'allow-list' and 'reply' not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Never set, never mutated, never inherited -- see the module docstring. A council that normalises a remote Ollama into a shared environment silently invalidates offload.py's trusted-lane justification repo-wide.
claims.why: References module docstring and offload.py not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A fresh, EMPTY temp directory to spawn a council subprocess in. Not the repo, not a worktree, containing no repo files. Returned as a context manager so the directory is fresh per call and removed after.
claims.why: The function returns tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, which is a context manager and creates a fresh empty temp directory.

claims.text: Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root, because a reviewer rooted in the checkout is the failure this exists to prevent.
claims.why: The function checks if the temp dir is inside repo_root and raises ValueError if so.

claims.text: THE PROMPT IS NEVER IN argv. It is staged to a temp file and handed over as the child's stdin.
claims.why: The function writes stdin_text to a temp file and passes the file as stdin to the subprocess.

claims.text: A file rather than a pipe because a CLI that never drains stdin deadlocks the writer OUTSIDE every timeout -- and because on the ssh path a command-line prompt is re-parsed by the remote login shell, which turns any backtick or $(...) in a diff into remote code execution with no adversarial model required.
claims.why: References ssh path and remote login shell behavior not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: The whole process TREE dies on timeout. Popen.terminate reaches the immediate child only; a hung vendor's grandchildren outlive it.
claims.why: The function calls proc.cancel() which is from ManagedProcess; the behavior of cancel (whether it kills the process tree) is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Fail closed: a child we could not contain must never be left running.
claims.why: The except block returns a RunResult with spawn_error but does not explicitly kill any child process; the guarantee relies on ManagedProcess context manager cleanup.

claims.text: args never contains the prompt: stdin_prompt is always true here and the shape is enforced by test, not by convention.
claims.why: References tests not present in this chunk.

claims.text: workspace-write and dontAsk are the two flags that turn a reviewer into an agent with an editor.
claims.why: The comment lists two examples but the tuple includes many more; the claim about 'two flags' is not fully verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: the denial is expressed with the = form, which cannot slurp.
claims.why: The comment explains that --allowed-tools would swallow next flag if empty, so they use --disallowed-tools=... form.

claims.text: ask is the ONLY entry point, and it always: charges the token ceiling, runs the secret floor, computes withheld paths for an untrusted lane, times the call, and maps every failure onto STATUSES. A refusal is a STATUS, not an exception -- a council must never lose a participant to a traceback, because a missing turn is indistinguishable from a turn that was never sought.
claims.why: The ask method and STATUSES are not defined in this chunk.

observations.what: floor_check docstring warns about a pattern (secret_floor_rule("", prompt)) that is not present in the function's code; the function itself uses it only as a backstop after per-file checks.
run_managed's except block for CancellationUnavailable and OSError does not attempt to kill the child process; relies on ManagedProcess context manager cleanup.
council_cwd only checks repo_root containment when repo_root is not None; if None, no check is performed.
CouncilAdapter docstring claims ask is the ONLY entry point, but ask method is not defined in this chunk.
FORBIDDEN_ARG_FRAGMENTS comment mentions 'two flags' but tuple contains many more; the comment may be misleading.
